q: Why was October close late, and which source system failed?

r.narrative: October is closing at WD+6: five working days faster than September (WD+11), but one day behind the WD+5 target. The source that failed again is the Business Central OData API. It timed out after 1.4M of 2.1M October journal lines. This time the ingestion agent switched automatically to paged extraction from the Data Lake replica and reconciled the result to the BC trial balance, so there was no manual workaround. In September, finance rebuilt the books from the Data Lake by hand over three days. The remaining day comes from 14 associated stores in Trøndelag and Nord-Norge whose legacy POS files arrived two days late, plus NOK 84.7M of unmatched items, mostly supplier invoices (NOK 29.9M) and store-owner intercompany (NOK 14.1M). Scope: October 2026 close · 12 feeds · NOK 1,357M under close.

rows: Timed out at 1.4M / 2.1M lines → Data Lake fallback

r.sql:
SELECT SOURCE_SYSTEM, FEED, STATUS, RECORDS_EXPECTED, RECORDS_LOADED, ROUND(RECORDS_LOADED / RECORDS_EXPECTED * 100, 1) AS COMPLETENESS_PCT, FALLBACK_USED
FROM SDP_SH_TEASER.PUBLIC.SH_CLOSE_INGESTION
WHERE CLOSE_PERIOD = '2026-10'
ORDER BY COMPLETENESS_PCT;

q: Which stores will run out of ski equipment before week 50?

r.narrative: Two stores run out of ski & winter stock before week 50 on the current plan: Intersport Trondheim City Syd (1.8 weeks of cover) and Solsiden (2.4 weeks) sell out in week 49, with NOK 6.2M of sales at risk. Three more sell out in week 50 itself: Sport 1 Oppdal, Sport 1 Steinkjer and Intersport Tromsø Jekta (ski boots). That makes five stores and NOK 10.4M of sales at risk (NOK 3.9M gross margin) by the start of the peak, NOK 8.6M of it in Trøndelag. The Gardermoen DC and three Oslo stores hold more than 9 weeks of cover on the same lines. Re-allocating 1,850 alpine and cross-country units before week 47 protects about NOK 7.1M of sales for about NOK 0.3M of transfer cost. Scope: FY2026 Q3 Forecast · all brands, stores and channels · NOK.
r.sql:
SELECT STORE_NAME, OWNERSHIP, STOCK_COVER_WEEKS, SELLOUT_WEEK, SALES_AT_RISK_NOK / 1e6 AS SALES_AT_RISK_M
FROM SDP_SH_TEASER.PUBLIC.SH_STOCK_COVER
WHERE CATEGORY = 'Ski & Winter' AND SELLOUT_WEEK < 51
ORDER BY SELLOUT_WEEK, STOCK_COVER_WEEKS;

q: What did stockouts cost us in lost gross margin YTD per brand?

r.narrative: Stockouts cost NOK 64.2M of sales and NOK 23.8M of gross margin from January to September. Intersport accounts for NOK 15.0M of the lost margin, Sport 1 for NOK 6.4M and Anton Sport for NOK 2.4M. Ski & winter is the largest category, followed by outdoor (summer stock in Vestland while East had excess) and running (sizes 42–44 in Oslo). On-shelf availability is 93.4% against a 96% target. The estimate compares ML store × category demand with on-shelf availability, after a substitution factor, so it is the same lost-margin figure finance and the stores see. Scope: FY2026 Q3 Forecast · all brands, stores and channels · NOK.
r.sql:
SELECT BRAND, SUM(LOST_SALES_NOK) / 1e6 AS LOST_SALES_M, SUM(LOST_GM_NOK) / 1e6 AS LOST_GM_M
FROM SDP_SH_TEASER.PUBLIC.SH_STOCKOUT_DAILY
WHERE SALES_DATE BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC;

q: Which promotions destroyed margin this year?

r.narrative: Two campaigns destroyed margin this year. The Anton Sport summer sale lifted units 14% but returned −NOK 4.1M of margin: 40% markdown depth on lifestyle footwear plus NOK 2.3M of media, and 61% of the volume was full-price demand pulled forward. The Intersport & Sport 1 summer sale returned −NOK 0.9M because it started in week 27, when demand was still full-price holiday shopping. Winter holiday (+NOK 4.1M), the spring running campaign (+NOK 2.3M) and member club days (+NOK 1.9M) were positive, so the year-to-date total is +NOK 3.3M. The ski season launch, the best-ROI campaign last year, runs now. Black Friday is planned at the same 40% depth for Anton Sport. Scope: FY2026 Q3 Forecast · all brands, stores and channels · NOK.
r.sql:
SELECT CAMPAIGN, BRAND, UNIT_UPLIFT_PCT, AVG_DEPTH_PCT, MARGIN_ROI_NOK / 1e6 AS MARGIN_ROI_M
FROM SDP_SH_TEASER.PUBLIC.SH_PROMO_ROI
WHERE FISCAL_YEAR = 2026
ORDER BY MARGIN_ROI_NOK;

q: Compare owned vs. associated store profitability.

r.narrative: Owned stores contribute 8.9% of sales (NOK 183M on NOK 2,061M) and associated stores 3.8% (NOK 144M on NOK 3,770M), after the store owners' management fee and profit share. Web shops add NOK 28M (2.9%) and Club & Team B2B NOK 10M. Gross margin is similar, at 39.0% for owned and 37.6% for associated stores. The difference is the store owners' share. Associated stores also tie up less group capital, because owners co-invest in fit-out and stock. Anton Sport (owned) has the highest store contribution at 7.7%, and associated Sport 1 stores the lowest at 3.6%. Scope: FY2026 Q3 Forecast · all brands, stores and channels · NOK.
r.sql:
SELECT OWNERSHIP, BRAND, SUM(NET_SALES) / 1e6 AS NET_SALES_M, SUM(CONTRIBUTION) / 1e6 AS CONTRIBUTION_M, SUM(CONTRIBUTION) / SUM(NET_SALES) * 100 AS CONTRIBUTION_PCT
FROM SDP_SH_TEASER.PUBLIC.SH_STORE_PNL
WHERE FISCAL_YEAR = 2026
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY CONTRIBUTION_PCT DESC;

q: What is the cost of waiting one more year to modernize our data platform?

r.narrative: On directional bands built from Sport Holding's own data, waiting one more year costs about NOK 41M net of Snowflake run cost, in a range of NOK 30–55M, or about NOK 3.4M a month. The largest items are stockout margin recovered (NOK 12.7M), lower external consultant dependency (NOK 8.4M), lower markdowns on aged stock (NOK 7.4M) and avoided margin-negative promotions (NOK 6.2M). Retiring the legacy platform and licence overlap adds NOK 4.2M, and close effort NOK 3.6M. These are directional estimates to build together with finance, not commitments. Each band shows its method and inputs so it can be challenged.

q: What would a 3-month pilot cost on Snowflake?

r.narrative: A 12-week (3-month) pilot on Close + Stockout costs an indicative NOK 0.9–1.3M. That is about NOK 0.15M of Snowflake consumption plus fixed-scope partner delivery with SWON. The pilot covers the Month-End Close Control Tower (Business Central, Omnium and Data Lake feeds with automatic fallback), Stockout Intelligence and the Store Manager Copilot in seven stores. Exit criteria: November close at WD+5 and ski stockouts in Trøndelag avoided. After the pilot, the annual Snowflake run cost is estimated at NOK 0.9–1.5M at list price. That covers ingestion and close on a Small warehouse, BI and self-service on a Medium warehouse in business hours, Cortex Analyst and agents, and about 15 TB of storage. Warehouses suspend automatically when idle and are billed per second. These are list-price indications to validate with the account team.
